chapter: New York bands and the first records
title: Harry Breuer and the drummer who copied his solos
summary: At NBC in New York he meets Harry Breuer, who had never thought of jazz on xylophone, and a young Rosenberg who had transcribed his Chicago solos.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And it was fun, though. Sammy Herman, used to get me -- he was a xylophone player, who was on NBC.
Had been on Lucky Strike, and Harry Brewer who used to listen to me in Chicago, when I was playing jazz with those Teatimers and the Blue Blazers and all --
And Harry told me that first time he heard

me he couldn't believe what he was hearing. That he didn't -- had never thought about playing jazz on it. Never entered it -- in his mind. Such a great player, a xylophone player, as Harry was. And he was on the Cliquet Club Eskimo, course I used to listen to him --

-- cause he was on the radio when I was in Minneapolis. So he had this Rosenberg boy who was a drummer who had per -- used to get up in the morning and listen to me and take down things that I played. So when I came to New York, before they went in the Biltmore, we were doing a radio show, we were in NBC on Fifth Avenue and -- oh, where was that, 5th Avenue 56th Street or 55th Street -- where NBC was.
And so we'd have a break, and I went into the next studio and here I recognized him. From his pictures in the advertisements and the magazines.

I recognized Harry Brewer and he was there, I didn't know this Rosenberg kid. So I had to set down. Well I was watching him and listening. Cause having -- never had any instructions on the instrument --
-- I was looking forward to coming to New York. Maybe I could --
From about the instrument because all the problems I'd had in learning, I -- just by trial and error.
I'd try hammering one way and then try another way. As a result it made me quite broad in the scope of what I could do.
But I'd try this way and I'd try that way and I just decided what is the correct way, like on the piano -- what is the correct way to finger --

So, I was sitting there and I left and went back to see if they needed me, so I went back and set down and finally this Rosenberg, I -- recognized me from something, I don't know what. And he told Harry, I saw him whisper to him, and he turned around, so that's when we became friends and he sat down and he said, I gotta play these for you. These are the things that he's taken off the air, the last -- I don't know whatever time we'd been on the air, from Chicago, he knows and here's some -- I made them into solos. And he played all about six solos. Scared me to death.
Cause I never knew what I was playing in those -- what jazz things I was -- I wasn't even thinking about --
